main_text.l: viciniores essent terrarum illi tractus,qui primos olim mortales Paradiso pulsos, & cum iis omnigenæ sapientiæ reliquias,ceu semina ex ceperunt, & ad posteros propagarunt. Etenim Adamum Protoplasten, post lamentabilem integritatis & felicitatis suæ iacturam,sapientiæ naturalis, quam innocenti creator infuderat, nobiles reliquias omniumque artium principia è Paradiso secum extulisse, & vicinis intulisse terris, posterisque communicasse, extra omne mihi dubium est. Accedebat, dubio procul,ingenii vigor, pro illo naturæ statu, maximus, experimenta, per annos DCCCCXXX[?] longè plurima & certissima; vt ab hoc velut oraculo vniuersus eruditi orbis posset.

Vtque certiori ac breviori via œcumenici huius primique Physiologi doctrina ad posteros transiret, vni auditori eius Mathusalæ, qui CCXLII annis ad Adami pedes federat in DCCCCLXIX annum vitam prorogavit. Methusalæ Noachus successit, anno Mundi MLVI, qui consuetudine & institutione præceptoris vti potuit, annis fere DC. Mundos Noachus hic, vt Hebræi distinguunt, annorum DCCCCLI spatio, tres vidit primum, ante diluvium, sub finem, longè

page.notes: Left margin note beside "Mathusalæ" is partly illegible; the third line of the note ("pulg") is uncertain and was read as "Adami filius". The "Noachus." marginal note is read as printed. "primos" appears split across lines without a visible hyphen, so it is written whole. "DCCCCXXX" is split across the line end as "DCC- / CCXXX"; the reading is uncertain. The catchword "gè" is taken from the lower right; the last line ends in "lon-" with a printed hyphen.
